messages:
Maya (Marketing): Quick pulse — poll closed. Top pick: 'Practical inference economics: tradeoffs, benchmarks, and what actually moves buyer decisions' (46%). Second was 'deploy patterns for low-latency chat' at 28%. Can we lock this topic and move to abstracts + speaker confirmations?
Liam (PM): I'm good to MC and do a ~3min opener framing the problem. fine with Wed rehearsal 9am PT. :thumbsup:
Sasha (Content): I can draft two micro-abstracts (1 x 30s for landing page, 1 x 90s for speaker prep) and a 3-slide TL;DR. Posting first draft in 30m.
Noah (Demand Gen): Super. For promotion cadence: 2 weeks out announce + benchmark tease, 1 week out technical deep-dive CTA, 2 days out reminder. I'll map channels after abstract final.
Maya (Marketing): Speaker ask: @Liam confirm you can share the 1-slide model-econ chart (cost vs latency). @Sasha will you own the benchmark narrative + sample prompts we'll show?
Liam (PM): Yes — I have the chart. Can simplify to 1 axis: $/1000 tokens vs p50 latency.
Sasha (Content): On it. Will create a short prompt set (3 prompts) that highlights batching and caching impact. Will annotate expected metric delta.
Maya (Marketing): Rehearsal plan idea: 20min talk (12min content + 8min demo/benchmarks), 10min panel Q&A. 60min run block for greenroom to test mics, screenshare, and demo fallbacks. Thoughts?
Noah (Demand Gen): +1. For demos, we need a non-prod endpoint and a static fallback screenshot if live infer goes sideways. I'll provision the test key and host a static image.
Sasha (Content): Draft abstract (30s): "Join Redwood Inference for a practical session on inference economics — how batching, caching, and model selection translate to real unit-cost wins without sacrificing latency. Includes live benchmarks and a short troubleshooting checklist." Feedback?
Liam (PM): Clean. Maybe add one sentence about who should attend (platform/infra/product).
Maya (Marketing): Good call — add: "For platform, infra, and product teams running LLM features."
Sasha (Content): Updated and uploaded to Google Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-link (will replace with final).
Maya (Marketing): Run-of-show (first-pass) — paste below. Please comment inline.
Sasha (Content): ```
00:00 - 00:30  intro (Maya)
00:30 - 03:30  problem framing + buyer pain (Liam)
03:30 - 09:30  benchmark methodology + demo (Liam + Sasha)
09:30 - 12:30  practical controls (batching, caching, quant) (Sasha)
12:30 - 18:00  live compare: config A vs B (Liam demo)
18:00 - 20:00  TL;DR + next steps (Maya)
20:00 - 30:00  moderated Q&A
30:00 - 60:00  greenroom: post-event ask & follow-ups (internal)
```
Liam (PM): Looks good. For the demo segment: add a fallback slide at 07:00 that shows pre-computed numbers and screenshots.
Noah (Demand Gen): For registrations form, add a question: "Primary role" and "Main inference pain" so we can route follow-ups.
Maya (Marketing): Logistics: can we tentatively book Wed 9am PT for the tech rehearsal and Fri 9am PT for the full dress? If that works I'll send invites.
Liam (PM): Wed + Fri booked for me.
Sasha (Content): Wed works. Friday might be tight but I'll make it.
GreenroomBot: Event created: "Practical inference economics" — Tech rehearsal Wed 2024-02-07 09:00 PT, Dress Fri 2024-02-09 09:00 PT. Calendar links sent to participants.
Maya (Marketing): Action list: 1) Sasha: publish final 30s + 90s abstracts by EOD tomorrow; 2) Liam: prepare chart + precomputed numbers; 3) Noah: create regs form + test key + static fallback; 4) Maya: invites + recording ops. Mark done here when complete.
Liam (PM): Will mark when chart uploaded.
Sasha (Content): Drafts uploaded by EOD.
Noah (Demand Gen): Test key provisioned and static fallback hosted at https://cdn.redwood.fake/fallback.png
Maya (Marketing): Perfect — I'll assemble slide deck and share a single link for review. Thanks team :rocket:
